- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SqliteWasmDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via SqliteWasmDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `37ca8c03e2fccf0d2e305cce812a8c521a0eed47` — the merge of head `ebb76076a8ef6cd568a463dcfb58bd1974e41849` into base `a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 37ca8c03e2fccf0d2e305cce812a8c521a0eed47 && git checkout 37ca8c03e2fccf0d2e305cce812a8c521a0eed47
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d ebb76076a8ef6cd568a463dcfb58bd1974e41849 && git checkout -B drift-repro a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d && git merge --no-ff ebb76076a8ef6cd568a463dcfb58bd1974e41849

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a46efa8c625f2b43d4aa1aa1044eb702667ba07d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a37e3c5f2c6dc9c872ca401eacc4a0abe4627f09`
Local-runs: none

PR #37450 (card #37429), declaration face, `Clause-②: no`. Read: the card and all four comments, the PR body and comments, the net diff (+97 −1, 3 files), the head's check-runs, and source at the head (`sqlite-wasm-driver.ts`, `wasm-connection.ts`, `knex-wasm-dialect.ts`, `sql-driver-lifecycle.ts`, tarn 3.1.2 `Pool.js` and `PendingOperation.js`, knex 3.3.0 `client.js`, `packages/core/src/kernel.ts`, the datasource connection service). Nothing was built or run; every statement below about runtime behaviour is from reading code, and every statement about a test result is the dev's report or a check-run conclusion.

Check-runs at this head: 53 completed, 0 failure. `Test Core` and its ten shards, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are `success`. The `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix shards are `skipped` on this head (the aggregate is `success`), so no check-run exercised the dogfood file here. The 20/20 repeat, the ablation and the 6 s-fsync repro are dev-reported (PR body, os-dev-report 7183856403), not gate verdicts.

### ① Derived judgments

**Root cause: right, as far as code reading can confirm.**
- `destroyRawConnection` calls `connection.close()` (`knex-wasm-dialect.ts:221-222`), and `close()` awaits the final `flush()` (`wasm-connection.ts:551-571`).
- tarn wraps that destroyer in `new PendingOperation(this.destroyTimeoutMillis)`, default 5000 (`Pool.js:74`, `:444`). A timeout goes to `_logDestroyerError` and the chain resolves (`:455-465`). `Pool.destroy()` is wrapped in `reflect`, so `knex.destroy()` resolves too.
- So before the fix `disconnect()` returned at "flush done or 5 s". The 5.005 s rollback-to-eviction gap the card quotes from CI run 45751259665 matches that constant. I did not re-read the CI log.
- Before the fix the same path also swallowed a FAILED final flush: tarn logged it as `destroyFail` and `disconnect()` resolved.

**Awaiting flush in `disconnect()`: correct on the main path.**
- Ordering and double flush: the driver's `flush()` acquires the connection, runs `conn.flush()`, releases, then `super.disconnect()` destroys the pool. The second flush inside `close()` finds `dirty === false` and returns without an export (`wasm-connection.ts:441`). There is no flush after destroy: `conn.flush()` returns early once `destroyed` is set (`:429`).
- Background flushes under `on-write`: `conn.flush()` appends to `flushChain`, so the awaited step runs after every queued step. A failed earlier step leaves `dirty` set and this step retries it.
- Error path: `try { flush } finally { super.disconnect() }` releases the pool whether or not the flush throws, then rethrows the flush error. If `super.disconnect()` itself threw it would replace the flush error; tarn's `reflect` makes that unlikely. The error surfaces instead of being swallowed. Every in-repo caller I found catches it and logs: `datasource-connection-service.ts:979-983` and `:1126-1130` (warn), `engine-migration-state.ts:463-467` (error), `sqlite-driver-fallback.ts:195-199`, and the two plugin `destroy()` wrappers. A refused boot therefore still rejects with its original cause.
- Called twice in sequence: after the first call knex sets `client.pool = undefined` (`client.js:524`), so `hasLiveConnection()` is false, no flush is attempted and `knex.destroy()` is a no-op. Safe.
- Racing an in-flight write: the pool is `{ min: 1, max: 1 }`, so the flush's acquire queues behind the write and sees its result. This is better than before. Because the acquire only returns a released connection, `conn.flush()` is not reached with `inTransaction` set by a live caller.
- `hasLiveConnection()` counts `numFree + numUsed` only. A driver that never connected is left alone, as the comment says. A connection still in `pendingCreates` is missed and falls back to the old 5 s path; no writes can exist on it yet.

S1 (should-fix) — the error path has no test. The changeset publishes "a flush that fails is thrown from `disconnect()`", and before this PR that failure was swallowed by tarn. Nothing pins the new contract: that `disconnect()` rejects on a failed final flush AND that the pool is released first. A follow-up test in `sqlite-wasm-driver-durability.test.ts` would do it. Not blocking: the code reads correct and all callers catch.

S2 (should-fix) — a second `disconnect()` that overlaps the first call's pool teardown can stall for knex's acquire timeout and then reject. Read, not run. While the first call is inside `pool.destroy()`, `client.pool` is still set and `free` still holds the connection (`Pool.js:228` clears it last), so `hasLiveConnection()` is true. The second call's `flush()` then asks a pool with `destroyed === true` for a connection; `_tryAcquireOrCreate` returns at once (`Pool.js:255-256`), and the pending acquire sits until the acquire timeout (knex default 60000 ms, `client.js:252-262`; the driver sets none). Before the fix the second call went straight to `knex.destroy()`. The window is short in the normal case and the kernel's teardown loops are sequential, so I found no in-repo caller that hits it. A one-line guard (skip the flush when `pool.destroyed`, or share one in-flight disconnect promise) closes it. Follow-up, not blocking.

**Can the await hang shutdown indefinitely: yes, by design, and the outer bound depends on the path.**
- The flush leg has no timeout of its own. The acquire leg is bounded by knex's 60 s acquire timeout. The file write, `fsync` and rename are unbounded.
- A graceful `shutdown()` is bounded by the kernel's `shutdownTimeout`. A refused boot's `rollbackStartedPlugins()` has no timeout (`kernel.ts:1052-1068`), so a `fsync` that never returns now holds `bootStack`'s rejection open. Before the fix that leg ended at 5 s.
- This is not a new class of hang: `Pool.destroy()` already waits without bound for used connections (`Pool.js:208`). I accept the trade: the old bound bought a silent durability loss, and the changeset states "with no timeout".

N1 (nit) — the code comment says "awaited HERE, with no timeout" but not what bounds it from outside. One sentence naming `shutdownTimeout`, and that the rollback path has none, would save the next reader the search.

**Other drivers: the pattern is not shared; no card owed.**
- `SqlDriver.disconnect()` is `knex.destroy()` alone (`sql-driver-lifecycle.ts:415-417`). Native better-sqlite3 commits to the file at write time, so its destroyer carries no deferred durable work.
- `TursoDriver.disconnect()` clears the sync interval, closes the libSQL client synchronously and calls `super.disconnect()` (`turso-driver.ts:2468-2489`). It runs no final `sync()` at disconnect, so there is nothing for tarn to cut short. Whether an embedded replica SHOULD sync on disconnect is a separate product question, not this defect.
- memory, mongodb and odata do not go through a Knex destroyer. `driver-sqlite-wasm` is the only `destroyRawConnection` that does durable work.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`: agreed. The `Check Changeset` run is `success`.
- No exported signature changes. `disconnect()` and `flush()` still take no argument and return a void promise; `hasLiveConnection()` is `private`. No config key is added, removed or re-defaulted.
- Behaviour changes, both stated in the changeset: `disconnect()` may now take longer than 5 s, and it may now reject where it used to resolve (a failed final flush). The second is the one a consumer could observe as new. It moves the driver toward what its own log text already promised ("close() throws if it still fails"), and it removes a silent data loss, so `patch` is the right level and no BREAKING banner is owed. Nothing an author can write is widened or narrowed, so `Clause-②: no` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Out-of-PR observation on `rollbackStartedPlugins`: a real asymmetry, worded wrongly in the PR, and it needs a card.**
- `performShutdown()` destroys EVERY plugin that has a `destroy` (`kernel.ts:1113-1123`). `rollbackStartedPlugins()` destroys only names in `startedPlugins` (`:1053`), and a name gets there only when the plugin has a `start` and it succeeded (`:1011-1013`, `:1028`).
- So on a failed boot three groups keep whatever `init()` acquired: a plugin with `init` and `destroy` but no `start`; the plugin whose own `start()` failed or timed out; and every plugin when the boot fails before any `start()` succeeds (the catch at `:664-672` requires a non-empty `startedPlugins`).
- The PR body's example is inaccurate: `DefaultDatasourcePlugin` is not init-only. It has `init` (`default-datasource-plugin.ts:143`), `start` (`:207`) and `destroy` (`:312`). It was skipped by this rollback only if its `start()` had not completed when the guard refused. The dev is right that this did not cause #37429, since the datasource-admin plugin's `destroy()` closed the default pool.

S3 (should-fix) — file a card on `packages/core` for the rollback/shutdown asymmetry above, with the three groups named, and correct the "init-only" wording when it is filed. Outside this PR's file surface, so correctly not fixed here. I did not search for an existing card; dedupe at filing.

**Timing robustness of the durability test: not flaky in the passing direction.**
- With the fix the assertion does not depend on any clock: `disconnect()` awaits the flush however long the patched `fsync` takes, and the `close()` flush inside the 50 ms destroyer is a no-op. A slow runner only makes the test slower (about 400 ms of added delay per fsync).
- Its power to fail without the fix rests on 400 ms exceeding 50 ms. A slow runner widens that margin. The red result on ablation (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'a1' ]`) is the dev's report; `Test Core` green at this head confirms only the passing direction.

N2 (nit) — the test patches `FileHandle.prototype.sync` for the whole worker and restores it in `afterEach`. That is safe with vitest's per-file isolation; it would leak a 400 ms fsync into neighbours if the package ever ran with `isolate: false`. A comment saying so is enough.

N3 (nit) — the test passes `pool` with `as any` to reach `destroyTimeoutMillis`. If a later change to the config path dropped that key, the test would keep passing with the fix and silently stop discriminating. Asserting the pool's effective `destroyTimeoutMillis` once would pin the premise.

**Card acceptance.** Root cause named on the card with evidence: met (7183113339). A test that fails without the fix: present, red-on-ablation as reported. Twenty repeated runs: dev-reported 20/20; no check-run at this head ran the dogfood shards, so the merge queue's Dogfood gate is the first CI measurement of that file on this change.

**SQL push-down.** Not applicable on any face of this diff: no query, id materialisation or in-app join is added. The change is connection lifecycle only.

No must-fix. S1, S2 and S3 are follow-ups that do not gate this head.

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `a37e3c5f2c6dc9c872ca401eacc4a0abe4627f09`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5: contract record 7184310941 reads PASS. The root cause and the fix hold. Three should-fix findings close before ACCEPT: one pin in this PR, and two that are this PR's or a card's.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 3 files (+97/−1), `Fixes #37429`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` patch. `l1-face` is CLEAN: 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed.
2. **Premise**: the dialect's destroyer runs the final flush inside `close()`, tarn bounds it at 5000 ms and resolves anyway, and `disconnect()` now awaits `flush()` itself inside a `try/finally` that releases the pool and rethrows. There is no double-flush or flush-after-destroy. Other drivers do not share the pattern. No SQL push-down question arises.
3. **Owed before ACCEPT**:
   - **S1.** The changeset publishes "a failed flush is thrown from `disconnect()`", but nothing pins it. Add a case: the flush rejects, `disconnect()` rejects with that error, and the pool is released first.
   - **S2.** A second `disconnect()` overlapping the first call's teardown can wait out knex's 60 s acquire timeout and then reject (read, not run; no in-repo caller does this). Either memoise the in-flight disconnect promise and pin it, or file a card under #37429 and say so in the changeset.
   - **S3.** File a card on `packages/core`: `rollbackStartedPlugins()` destroys only plugins whose `start()` succeeded, while `performShutdown()` destroys every plugin with a `destroy`. Correct the PR's wording too: `DefaultDatasourcePlugin` is not init-only.
   The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations**: the unbounded flush on the refused-boot rollback, by design (graceful shutdown stays capped by `shutdownTimeout`). Nits: N1 (the comment should name what bounds the await), N2 (the worker-wide `FileHandle.prototype.sync` patch relies on per-file isolation) and N3 (`destroyTimeoutMillis` reached through `as any`).
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: the rollback/shutdown asymmetry goes to the card S3 asks for, and the overlapping disconnect, if not fixed here, goes to the card S2 allows.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier. Owed: a same-head PASS with S1–S3 closed, then an **ACCEPT**, after which the area lands it. The Dogfood Regression Gate shards are `skipped` on this head, so the merge queue is the dogfood file's first CI run on this change. If the same signature returns there, stop and diagnose.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ebb76076a8ef6cd568a463dcfb58bd1974e41849`
Local-runs: none

Delta review of PR #37450 (card #37429), declaration face, `Clause-②: no`. Previous record: head `a37e3c5f2c6dc9c872ca401eacc4a0abe4627f09`, PASS with S1, S2, S3, N1, N2, N3. Read for this round: the diff between that head and this one (+91 −17, the same three files), the PR body at this head, delta comment 7184996590, os-dev-report 7184504855, and this head's check-runs. Nothing was built or run. Runtime statements are from reading code; test results are the dev's report or check-run conclusions.

Check-runs at this head: 57 completed, 39 success, 18 skipped, 0 failure, taking the newer run of each name. `Test Core` and its ten shards, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Check Changeset` are `success`. The `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix shards are still `skipped` here, so the dogfood file's 20/20 remains dev-reported and the merge queue is its first CI measurement.

### ① Derived judgments

S1: closed. A new test makes every `fsync` throw one named error and asserts `disconnect()` rejects with that same object, then that `knex.client.pool` is undefined. Read against the code: the connection's `flush()` rethrows the error unchanged, the `finally` runs `super.disconnect()`, tarn swallows the destroyer's repeat failure, and the first error is rethrown. Both halves of the published contract are pinned.

S2: closed. `disconnect()` now returns a memoised `disconnecting` promise built from `disconnectOnce()`, cleared in `.finally` once it settles.
- A call that arrives during the first teardown gets the same promise, so it never reaches `flush()` on a destroyed pool.
- A call after it settles finds `client.pool` undefined, skips the flush, and runs a no-op `knex.destroy()`, as before.
- A rejected disconnect rejects every sharer with the same error, and the memo still clears, so a later call is not stuck on a stale rejection.
- The pin holds the destroyer, waits for `pool.destroyed`, calls `disconnect()` again and requires both to settle in under 2 s. The dev reports the memo ablation turns it red with a 10 s test timeout; that matches what the code predicts (a pending acquire on a destroyed pool until knex's 60 s timeout). I did not run it.

N4 (nit) — the overlap test's comments say the destroyer is held "for 300 ms" and that the pair settles in "about 300 ms". The pool in that test has `destroyTimeoutMillis: 50`, so tarn stops waiting at 50 ms and the window in which the second call can meet a destroyed pool is about 50 ms, polled every 5 ms. The test cannot fail spuriously with the fix. On a runner that stalls the poll past 50 ms it would pass without the memo too, so it loses discriminating power there, not correctness. Either give that test its own pool with a destroy timeout above the hold, or correct the comments.

N1: closed. The comment now names `shutdownTimeout` as the graceful bound and says the failed-boot rollback has none, with the reason.

Unchanged from the previous record and still held at this head: the root cause, the flush-then-destroy ordering, the no-op second flush inside `close()`, the in-flight-write case, and that no other driver shares the pattern.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: still agreed. `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- `disconnect()` dropped the `async` keyword but still takes no argument and returns a void promise. `disconnecting` and `disconnectOnce()` are `private`. No export or config key moves.
- The changeset gained one sentence for the shared-teardown behaviour, so all three observable changes are now stated: may exceed 5 s, may reject on a failed final flush, concurrent calls share one teardown. None widens or narrows what an author can write.

### ③ Boundary flags

S3: closed. The PR's acceptance note now says `DefaultDatasourcePlugin` has `init`, `start` and `destroy`, describes the rollback versus shutdown asymmetry correctly, and points at #37462.
